questions.prompt: What is the single non-negotiable rule of Clean Architecture?

options.text: There must be exactly four layers
Source-code dependencies must point only inward, toward higher-level policy
You must not use any framework

questions.explanation: The Dependency Rule — source-code dependencies point only inward — is the mandatory core. The number of layers is illustrative, and frameworks/interfaces are means, not the rule.

questions.prompt: According to Clean Architecture, which of these are 'details' the core should be independent of? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: The database, UI, and frameworks are volatile details kept at the edge. The business rules are the core value the architecture protects, not a detail.

questions.prompt: The rule that source-code dependencies may point only inward is called the ______ Rule.
questions.explanation: The Dependency Rule is the defining constraint of Clean Architecture.

questions.prompt: Order the four example layers from innermost (highest-level) to outermost (lowest-level).
questions.explanation: From the core outward: Entities (enterprise rules), Use Cases (application rules), Interface Adapters (controllers/presenters/gateways), then Frameworks & Drivers (the volatile outside).

questions.prompt: Match each architecture to the person who created it.
questions.explanation: These three are related but distinct: Clean (Martin), Hexagonal/Ports & Adapters (Cockburn), and Onion (Palermo). Attribute each correctly.

questions.prompt: Does 'independent of frameworks' mean a Clean Architecture app avoids frameworks entirely?

options.text: No — you still use frameworks, but keep them at the outer edge as replaceable details
Yes — you must write everything from scratch
No — because frameworks are part of the entities layer

questions.explanation: You still use frameworks; the point is to keep them in the outer ring as replaceable details rather than building your business rules inside them.
